Abstract

Let K/QpK/\mathbf Q_pK/Qp​ be finite with its prescribed absolute value. On an ordinary open in a good Hausdorff boundaryless quasi-smooth KKK-analytic space, we prove that the actual difference of two locally bounded classical plurisubharmonic functions with equal original CLD curvature is continuous and classically pluriharmonic. It follows that their relative curvatures agree for every fixed symmetric original-positive separately d′d'd′- and d′′d''d′′-closed background current. The mixed bounded Bedford–Taylor calculus therefore descends in its differentiated slots to currents with bounded classical local potentials.

The proof supplies the two gates left open in the fourth record: kernel preservation after every complete scalar extension and ordinary continuity of the actual curvewise harmonic difference. The first uses prescribed smooth rows, finite-etale traces, full analytic fiber potentials including type IV, and a simultaneous product induction. The second uses a Shilov bound proved without ambient semicontinuity, polynomial Noether coordinates, and exact logarithmic interpolation on strictly semistable alteration charts. All equalities are tested on the full original CLD test sheaf. Explicit scope tests exclude weaker closedness, arbitrary bounded upper-semicontinuous representatives, and an unrestricted passage to relative energy or capacitary completions. The previously proved seven fixed-background BT properties are retained as inputs. An exact global finite-dimensional curvature hypothesis yields local uniform compactness of normalized classical potentials. Without that hypothesis, a two-intersection example shows that the relative classical image can fail to be closed in total variation even when no boundary values are prescribed.

Reading guide

The exact main theorem and its short final proof are in Section “The arbitrary-background potential quotient”. The new analytic and geometric arguments are in Sections “Complete scalar extensions through one-variable fiber potentials”–“Algebraic neighborhoods for the continuity argument”. Section “The question, conventions, and frozen inputs” declares the inputs and the point-value and test-form conventions. Section “Status change from R4 and remaining proof boundaries” compares the current status with R4. The later examples distinguish false extensions from the stated theorem.

This is a focused continuation. It contains the new proofs rather than reprinting all 304 pages of R4. The complete archive retains the exact frozen R4 archive, its original internal inputs, all modular and stand-alone R5 LaTeX sources, source-location records, independent reading records, and the continuation handoff. References beginning “R4–” are numbered results in that frozen final record. Historical open statements in R4 are superseded only in the precise scopes stated here.

The question, conventions, and frozen inputs

The question left open in the fourth record was

D[u]=D[v]⟹D((u−v)S)=0,u,v∈Cb(U),D[u]=D[v]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad D((u-v)S)=0, \qquad u,v\in\mathcal C_b(U),D[u]=D[v]⟹D((u−v)S)=0,u,v∈Cb​(U),

for an arbitrary fixed symmetric positive separately closed background current SSS. The equality on the left is an equality of original CLD currents with background [1][1][1]. It must not be silently interpreted as equality after multiplication by a singular coefficient measure. The actual point values of uuu and vvv matter on the right.

The original ground field throughout the main theorem is a finite extension K/QpK/\mathbf Q_pK/Qp​ with its given absolute value. An allowed space is good, Hausdorff, boundaryless, quasi-smooth, and of pure dimension. All opens are ordinary topological opens. We set D=d′d′′D=d'd''D=d′d′′. A (p,p)(p,p)(p,p)-current on a space of dimension nnn acts on original compact smooth (n−p,n−p)(n-p,n-p)(n−p,n−p)-forms. Unless a different degree is explicitly stated, positivity is the original positive cone of R, namely the symmetric quadratic-form cone of [CLD12, Definition 5.1.1(c) and §5.4]. It is not identified with either strong or weak positivity.

The coefficient-Radon arguments use this middle cone directly. They do not invoke the strong-test order-zero assertion as printed in [CLD25, Proposition 7.2.9]. Section “A closed weakly positive tropical current need not have order zero” gives an explicit closed real-tropical counterexample to that broader assertion and checks the distinct 2012 hypotheses. This does not change R’s stipulated cone or any of the authorized internal inputs.

The word actual means that no function is replaced on a null, polar, or coefficient-null set. For a locally bounded Borel function aaa and a coefficient-Radon current TTT, multiplication means ⟨aT,η⟩=∫a dμT,η\langle aT,\eta\rangle =\int a\,d\mu_{T,\eta}⟨aT,η⟩=∫adμT,η​ on the actual Berkovich space. A measure specified only on one tropical image does not give this operation.

Authorized internal results

INTERNAL_INPUT: R.

R provides the continuous original-positive local calculus over the original field, its continuous semipositive smoothing, the original positive-cone coefficient-Radon controls, and compatibility of weak convergence of original-positive currents with a fixed continuous multiplier. Its statements use the original test category. Its local algebraic tube construction is used only over the original field, after B’s algebraic localization.

INTERNAL_INPUT: B.

B, Definition 2.2, defines Cb(U)\mathcal C_b(U)Cb​(U) by actual local boundedness, upper semicontinuity, and subharmonic pullbacks along every analytic curve after every complete isometric field extension. Theorem 2.5 gives decreasing continuous rational semipositive PL rows on one fixed ordinary neighborhood. Proposition 4.5 and the pure-Fubini–Study smoothing used in its construction give the prescribed smooth positive rows needed here. Explicitly, if pj↓up_j\downarrow upj​↓u and ∣sj−pj∣≤εj|s_j-p_j|\leq\varepsilon_j∣sj​−pj​∣≤εj​ with εj+1≤εj/4\varepsilon_{j+1}\leq\varepsilon_j/4εj+1​≤εj​/4, then sj+2εj↓us_j+2\varepsilon_j\downarrow usj​+2εj​↓u because its values lie between pj+εjp_j+\varepsilon_jpj​+εj​ and pj+3εjp_j+3\varepsilon_jpj​+3εj​. The original smooth curvatures stay positive. The fixed domain, rather than a separate shrinking domain for every jjj, is essential. B, Lemma D.4, supplies ordinary affine algebraic neighborhoods. B, Appendix A.2, supplies the positive Radon Laplacian and its original scalar-test identity on smooth algebraic curves over every complete nontrivially valued field of characteristic zero; that particular curve statement has the larger field range explicitly stated in B.

INTERNAL_INPUT: A2.

The same-model geometric adelic nefness result is already complete under its stated arithmetic and boundary assumptions. It is not used to prove the local quotient and is not counted as an open problem or a result of this round.

No comprehensive proof audit of R, B, or A2 has been undertaken. The checks concern their statements, fields, positivity cones, test categories, and dependencies.

The initial statement D[u]=D[v]D[u]=D[v]D[u]=D[v] is never pulled back as an arbitrary current. Each transfer theorem proves equality for the actual composed potentials, on every original test on the new space. The distinction is indispensable.

Logical structure of the new argument

The analytic part extends the prescribed-row finite-etale kernel argument to auxiliary complete fields. A continuous potential for the full analytic fiber of every nonrigid point of the affine line then closes the scalar-extension gate, including type IV. The product kernel is propagated simultaneously in every finite product dimension. The resulting analytic-map kernel gives actual harmonicity on all curve pullbacks, including their type-I and type-IV values.

The geometric part does not assume that a curvewise harmonic function is upper semicontinuous. It proves its Shilov bound by finite flat coordinates and normalized algebraic curve slices. Strictly semistable alteration charts supply continuous logarithmic interpolation of their finite Shilov data. The Shilov bound identifies the actual function with those interpolants, and proper compact descent proves continuity.

Only after that argument are both signs of u−vu-vu−v known to be classical psh. Applying the existing first-order positive construction to the arbitrary background SSS makes D((u−v)S)D((u-v)S)D((u−v)S) and its negative positive, which proves (eq:r5-main-question). The quotient is therefore downstream of all the kernel and continuity arguments.

Status convention.

NEW_PROVED means that a complete argument is supplied in this project relative to the declared inputs. It does not claim worldwide priority, external refereeing, or formal verification. It is distinct from DIRECT_COROLLARY, INTERNAL_INPUT, and EXTERNAL_KNOWN. The logical statuses are PROVED, CONDITIONAL, OPEN, and FALSE; an invalid proof mechanism is labeled FAILED_ATTEMPT.

Field-independent tools for prescribed smooth positive rows

Let FFF be a complete non-Archimedean field with its given absolute value. Let UUU be a good Hausdorff boundaryless FFF-analytic space of pure dimension n≥1n\geq1n≥1. We use only the original CLD smooth forms, their canonical integration, and D=d′d′′D=d'd''D=d′d′′. A current is positive in the original positive cone used in R, and all currents called positive below are symmetric. This is not a convention identifying the positive, strongly positive and weakly positive cones.

A prescribed smooth positive row for a function uuu on an ordinary open OOO means original smooth functions uju_juj​ on that same OOO, with positive (1,1)(1,1)(1,1)-forms DujDu_jDuj​, such that uju_juj​ decreases pointwise to the actual finite locally bounded function uuu. Whenever a continuous potential is used below, its smooth positive approximation is likewise part of the hypotheses. No regularization theorem over FFF is asserted. In particular, these results may be applied to rows already obtained over the original finite extension of Qp\mathbf Q_pQp​ and then pulled back by an analytic map or by scalar extension.

If Tj→TT_j\to TTj​→T weakly and all these currents are positive, then aTj→aTaT_j\to aTaTj​→aT for every fixed continuous multiplier aaa. Status: DIRECT_COROLLARY of the original finite-dimensional positive-cone controls and Radon representation. The proof below records why this part has no restriction to a discretely valued or locally compact ground field.

Proof. Localize the test into finitely many ordinary moment presentations with compact support. On one such presentation write t=(log⁡∣g1∣,…,log⁡∣gr∣)t=(\log|g_1|,\ldots,\log|g_r|)t=(log∣g1​∣,…,log∣gr​∣), where the gig_igi​ are analytic units, and put β=∑ν=1rd′tν∧d′′tν.\beta=\sum_{\nu=1}^r d't_\nu\wedge d''t_\nu.β=ν=1∑r​d′tν​∧d′′tν​. In the usual signed identification of symmetric (q,q)(q,q)(q,q)-tensors with symmetric quadratic forms on ⋀qRr\bigwedge^q\mathbf R^r⋀qRr, βq/q!\beta^q/q!βq/q! is the identity matrix. On a fixed compact real presentation stage it therefore dominates, up to a finite constant, both signs of the symmetric coefficient tensor of η\etaη. With an original compact smooth cutoff χ\chiχ equal to one near that stage, this gives Cχβq±η≥0.C\chi\beta^q\pm\eta\geq0.Cχβq±η≥0. The control χβq\chi\beta^qχβq is strongly positive. The inequalities are in the original positive cone; they do not assume that η\etaη is strongly positive. Antisymmetric parts have zero pairing with the symmetric current.

For every nonnegative original smooth scalar bbb, positivity gives ∣⟨T,bη⟩∣≤C⟨T,bχβq⟩.|\langle T,b\eta\rangle| \leq C\langle T,b\chi\beta^q\rangle .∣⟨T,bη⟩∣≤C⟨T,bχβq⟩. Original smooth scalar functions separate points on each good affinoid neighborhood: the absolute values of analytic functions separate Berkovich points, and smooth real profiles constant near zero turn these into original smooth scalars. Their compact versions are uniformly dense in continuous compactly supported functions on a fixed compact neighborhood. This is the original scalar Stone–Weierstrass argument, valid over every complete FFF; see also [CLD25, Propositions 15.2.6–15.2.9]. Positivity and the displayed control extend the functionals uniquely to that continuous scalar space. Riesz representation gives the positive measure of the control and the signed measure of η\etaη, with the displayed domination. The finitely many pieces give (R).

Relations between forms and changes of presentation are compatible because the corresponding original scalar-tested functionals are identical; uniqueness of Radon measures preserves every such identity. The matrix inequalities pull back under common refinements, so adding scalar coordinates does not change the controls. Applying this argument to the finitely many coefficient basis forms gives the actual coefficient-Radon description. It also proves continuity of aTaTaT in the original test topology for locally bounded Borel aaa: on each fixed compact presentation, the coefficient norms of a test bound the pairing by its fixed control masses times sup⁡∣a∣\sup|a|sup∣a∣.

For the last assertion, weak convergence bounds the finitely many positive control masses. Approximate the fixed continuous scalar aaa uniformly on their compact support by original smooth scalars. For each smooth scalar the claimed convergence is the definition of weak convergence. Inequality (R) bounds the two approximation errors uniformly in jjj. Taking the approximation error to zero proves the assertion. No countable atlas or measure separability has entered the argument. ◻

One relative slot and exchange with a continuous slot

Scope of the package.

The field-independent ingredients are finite positive matrix controls, compact smooth scalar density, original Stokes, and the vanishing of top-degree form germs on proper analytic subsets. The only approximations of the potentials are the prescribed rows. These results supply the first-order analytic-divisor removal and continuous-slot exchange used in an original-test projection argument. They do not establish a bounded mixed calculus for arbitrary unknown potentials over FFF, the arbitrary-background potential quotient, or a new pullback operation for arbitrary currents.

Finite etale kernel transfer for prescribed smooth rows

Let FFF be a complete nontrivially valued field of characteristic zero. Its absolute value is fixed. All analytic spaces in this section are good, Hausdorff, boundaryless, and quasi-smooth of pure dimension. All forms and currents are in the original CLD sheaf. In particular, “positive” denotes the positive semidefinite cone, with no replacement by the weakly smooth or delta-form sheaf.

Definition (A prescribed smooth row). An actual locally bounded classical psh function aaa on an ordinary open UUU is said to have a prescribed smooth row if every point has one ordinary neighborhood VVV and original smooth functions aja_jaj​ on VVV such that aj↓aa_j\downarrow aaj​↓a pointwise and DajDa_jDaj​ is a positive (1,1)(1,1)(1,1)-form. The neighborhoods do not depend on jjj. The word “classical” retains the upper-semicontinuity and all-complete-extension curve conditions. Those conditions are not deduced from the current equation in this definition.

The functions occurring in the original problem have these rows by the authorized regularization in B, followed by smoothing its pure Fubini–Study presentations on a common smaller domain. Explicitly, if pj↓ap_j\downarrow apj​↓a are the continuous semipositive weights, choose smooth positive weights sjs_jsj​ with ∣sj−pj∣≤ϵj|s_j-p_j|\leq\epsilon_j∣sj​−pj​∣≤ϵj​, where ϵj+1≤ϵj/4\epsilon_{j+1}\leq\epsilon_j/4ϵj+1​≤ϵj​/4. Then sj+3ϵjs_j+3\epsilon_jsj​+3ϵj​ decrease and have limit aaa. The same fixed rows pull back to every complete extension and every analytic morphism: smooth pullback commutes with DDD, preserves positive (1,1)(1,1)(1,1)-forms, and preserves pointwise decrease. Classicality of the limit is already supplied by the original all-extension definition. This is a DIRECT_COROLLARY about specified rows; it is not a regularization theorem for all classical psh functions over FFF.

Lemma (Piecewise tests over an arbitrary complete field). Let η\etaη be a compactly supported finite original piecewise smooth (q,q)(q,q)(q,q)-test: in a finite unit-moment presentation it is piecewise smooth on a finite affine hyperplane arrangement, smooth up to each closed chamber, and its tangential restrictions agree on all common faces. If symmetric positive separately closed currents TjT_jTj​ of complementary bidegree converge to a symmetric positive separately closed current TTT on all original smooth tests, then ⟨Tj,η⟩⟶⟨T,η⟩.\langle T_j,\eta\rangle\longrightarrow\langle T,\eta\rangle.⟨Tj​,η⟩⟶⟨T,η⟩. The piecewise pairing uses the actual coefficient Radon measures and is independent of the chamber representatives chosen on the walls.

Here the Θb\Theta_bΘb​ are finitely many fixed positive compact smooth tests, and sup⁡jMj<∞\sup_jM_j<\inftysupj​Mj​<∞ by weak convergence. The same bound holds for TTT. Matrix Cauchy–Schwarz for the original positive cone therefore bounds every coefficient with one primed or double-primed normal factor on that tube by Cϵ1/2MjC\epsilon^{1/2}M_jCϵ1/2Mj​.

Convolve the ambient chamber tensors by a radius-ϵ\epsilonϵ real smooth kernel, then multiply by the fixed compact cutoff. This gives an original smooth ηϵ\eta_\epsilonηϵ​. On any one wall, tangential matching writes the branch difference as ℓθ+d′ℓ∧ξ+d′′ℓ∧ζ\ell\theta+d'\ell\wedge\xi+d''\ell\wedge\zetaℓθ+d′ℓ∧ξ+d′′ℓ∧ζ with uniformly bounded coefficients. For finitely many walls, subdivide a segment joining two points at distance at most ϵ\epsilonϵ by its wall crossings. The smooth variations along its chambers sum to O(ϵ)O(\epsilon)O(ϵ); each jump is in the corresponding normal ideal, and its wall is at distance O(ϵ)O(\epsilon)O(ϵ) from the initial point. Lemma (Finite etale trace in the original piecewise class). Let p:Z→Up:Z\to Up:Z→U be finite etale between the spaces above. The pushforward current of any compact original smooth form on ZZZ is represented locally on UUU by finite original compatible piecewise smooth forms. The identity holds on every original complementary test and every further original moment refinement.

Proof. The construction of Theorem R4–73.3 in R4 uses only the following operations, all valid over the present FFF. We recall the construction and the calibration rather than assuming a field-extension rule for currents.

Properness and finiteness allow one to shrink an ordinary base neighborhood until the source is a finite disjoint union of pieces carrying single moment presentations. Treat one such piece of rank ddd, with source units h1,…,hmh_1,\ldots,h_mh1​,…,hm​ and form ω(log⁡∣h1∣,…,log⁡∣hm∣)\omega(\log|h_1|,\ldots,\log|h_m|)ω(log∣h1​∣,…,log∣hm​∣). For each a∈{0,…,d}ma\in\{0,\ldots,d\}^ma∈{0,…,d}m, take the characteristic polynomial of ha=∏ihiaih^a=\prod_i h_i^{a_i}ha=∏i​hiai​​ in the finite locally free analytic algebra: Qa(T)=Td+ca,1Td−1+⋯+ca,d.Q_a(T)=T^d+c_{a,1}T^{d-1}+\cdots+c_{a,d}.Qa​(T)=Td+ca,1​Td−1+⋯+ca,d​. The roots over an algebraic closure of each completed residue field give the ddd geometric sheets with their full multiplicities. Their ordered logarithmic norms are the Newton-polygon slopes of QaQ_aQa​. On a fixed compact neighborhood all these norms are bounded by some BBB. A coefficient vanishing at the chosen base point can be omitted after shrinking until its norm is less than exp⁡(−dB−1)\exp(-dB-1)exp(−dB−1): it cannot lie on the lower Newton hull. The other coefficients are original analytic units after a further shrinking. Consequently the ordered root norms are finite continuous piecewise affine functions of finitely many original base unit logarithms.

These records determine the unordered vectors zl=(log⁡∣hi∣)iz_l=(\log|h_i|)_izl​=(log∣hi​∣)i​, including multiplicities. Indeed, the records determine ∏l=1d(X−a⋅zl)\prod_{l=1}^d(X-a\cdot z_l)∏l=1d​(X−a⋅zl​) on the grid {0,…,d}m\{0,\ldots,d\}^m{0,…,d}m; polynomial interpolation determines this polynomial in all its variables, and its monic linear factorization determines the vectors. All possible joint listings are obtained by permuting coordinate lists. Consistency is a finite system of linear equalities and inequalities. Thus on finitely many polyhedral cells one may list the vectors as affine maps zl(t)z_l(t)zl​(t) and set τ=∑l=1dzl∗ω.\tau=\sum_{l=1}^d z_l^*\omega.τ=l=1∑d​zl∗​ω. On common faces the unordered lists agree. A finite further subdivision fixes their matching permutations, so the forms have equal tangential restrictions. This construction initially gives a form on a finite closed polyhedral locus in real moment space. Triangulate this locus together with a larger box and barycentrically subdivide. On the neighborhood where the sum of hat functions of its vertices is greater than 1/21/21/2, their normalized barycentric combination retracts piecewise smoothly onto the locus. Pullback by this retraction extends τ\tauτ to a full real neighborhood of each compact moment image, preserving tangential compatibility. The resulting form is therefore an original piecewise test, not merely a form on an abstract skeleton.

For the current identity, use the finite-flat degree formula for calibrated skeletons: [Mih24, Lemma 3.15 and Proposition 3.19, especially equation (3.20)]. Those results are stated over an arbitrary complete non-Archimedean field. Their local weights are finite algebra degrees; they are not replaced by a product of value-group and residue-field degrees. Hence possible valued-field defect causes no omitted factor. Adjoining the source units does not increase graded transcendence degree, by their characteristic equations. Omitted coefficients are still strictly below the maximal terms of each initial equation, so the retained unit coefficients suffice for this assertion. The degree formula therefore gives, for every original complementary test γ\gammaγ on the base, ∫Zω(log⁡∣h∣)∧p∗γ=∫Uτ∧γ.\int_Z\omega(\log|h|)\wedge p^*\gamma =\int_U\tau\wedge\gamma.∫Z​ω(log∣h∣)∧p∗γ=∫U​τ∧γ. It remains valid after every extra base moment refinement. The extension off the consistent real locus contributes nothing on the actual calibrated cells. There is no additional wall current. Finite partitions and Lemma “Piecewise tests over an arbitrary complete field” complete the construction and its independence statements. ◻

Theorem (Finite etale preservation for prescribed rows). Let p:Z→Up:Z\to Up:Z→U be finite etale, and let u,vu,vu,v be actual locally bounded classical psh functions on UUU, each with prescribed smooth rows. If D[u]=D[v]D[u]=D[v]D[u]=D[v] on all original tests on UUU, then D[u∘p]=D[v∘p]D[u\circ p]=D[v\circ p]D[u∘p]=D[v∘p] on all original tests on ZZZ.

Status: NEW_PROVED field extension of the R4 finite-etale argument, relative to the stated coefficient lemma. No regularization of new functions over FFF is asserted.

Proof. Let α∈Acn−1,n−1(Z)\alpha\in A_c^{n-1,n-1}(Z)α∈Acn−1,n−1​(Z). Choose a finite original smooth partition on a neighborhood of its projected compact support, subordinate to ordinary neighborhoods carrying rows for both uuu and vvv. Replace α\alphaα in turn by (p∗χ)α(p^*\chi)\alpha(p∗χ)α for the members χ\chiχ of this partition. It suffices by linearity to treat each resulting test, whose projected support now lies in one common row neighborhood. For such a test, still denoted by α\alphaα, put P=p∗[α]P=p_*[\alpha]P=p∗​[α] and ν=DP=p∗[Dα]\nu=DP=p_*[D\alpha]ν=DP=p∗​[Dα]. The latter is one fixed signed Radon measure of compact support. By the preceding lemma, PPP is represented on a finite compact cover by compatible original piecewise tests. Take the given bounded smooth decreasing rows uj,vju_j,v_juj​,vj​ on the chosen neighborhood of the projected support. Their positive separately closed curvatures converge to the same current, by fixed smooth-test dominated convergence. Lemma “Piecewise tests over an arbitrary complete field” gives ⟨P,D(uj−vj)⟩⟶0.\langle P,D(u_j-v_j)\rangle\longrightarrow0.⟨P,D(uj​−vj​)⟩⟶0. Compact smooth Stokes identifies this expression with ∫(uj−vj) dν\int(u_j-v_j)\,d\nu∫(uj​−vj​)dν. Bounded convergence against this fixed measure identifies its limit with ∫(u−v) dν=⟨D[(u−v)∘p],α⟩.\int(u-v)\,d\nu =\langle D[(u-v)\circ p],\alpha\rangle.∫(u−v)dν=⟨D[(u−v)∘p],α⟩. Sum the finitely many localized identities. The derivatives in DαD\alphaDα include those of the fixed partitioned test; no derivative of a partitioned potential is taken. This proves the equality on the arbitrary original test without assuming a global row. ◻

Corollary (Finite scalar extensions). If F′/FF'/FF′/F is finite, the same prescribed pair satisfies D[uF′]=D[vF′]D[u_{F'}]=D[v_{F'}]D[uF′​]=D[vF′​] on all original F′F'F′-tests.

Proof. Characteristic zero makes the scalar extension map finite etale. Apply the theorem with UF′U_{F'}UF′​ viewed as an FFF-space. Its original analytic functions, moment tests, and their topology are the same in both interpretations. Its integration current in the FFF-calibration is [F′:F][F':F][F′:F] times its integration current in the F′F'F′-calibration. This is the finite-constant formula of CLD, also checked directly in Mihatsch, Lemma 3.16. Dividing by this single positive degree proves the assertion. The different scalar pushforward formula has factor one; it is not being substituted for the present same-space calibration. ◻

Complete scalar extensions through one-variable fiber potentials

The original finite extension K/QpK/\mathbf Q_pK/Qp​ keeps its given absolute value. Auxiliary complete fields below always carry extending absolute values. Tests are original CLD forms. The new-field input is the prescribed-row finite-etale kernel theorem “Finite etale preservation for prescribed rows”, with the coefficient control of Lemma lem:r5-prescribed-coefficient-control. Neither a regularization theorem for arbitrary psh functions over an auxiliary field nor the arbitrary-background potential quotient is used in this section.

Here a prescribed smooth row for uuu means a sequence of original smooth functions uj↓uu_j\downarrow uuj​↓u, locally uniformly bounded, with positive (1,1)(1,1)(1,1)-curvature forms. When such a row is pulled back by scalar extension, the smooth forms remain positive: in an original moment presentation their pullbacks are the pullbacks of the same positive quadratic forms under linear maps of tangent spaces. The extra moment directions introduced by a refinement cause no change to this argument. Thus the rows supplied over the original KKK are used as specified functions over later fields; no new regularization assertion over those fields is inferred. All row arguments are local on fixed ordinary algebraic neighborhoods.

Exchange with a continuous potential needs only a prescribed row

Lemma (Continuous-slot exchange over an auxiliary field). Let FFF be a complete non-Archimedean field, let WWW be a good Hausdorff boundaryless quasi-smooth FFF-analytic space, and suppose uuu has a prescribed smooth row on WWW. Let bbb be continuous and suppose D[b]D[b]D[b] is a symmetric original-positive current. Then D(uD[b])=D(bD[u]).D\bigl(uD[b]\bigr)=D\bigl(bD[u]\bigr).D(uD[b])=D(bD[u]). All products here are multiplication of coefficient-Radon currents by the displayed actual Borel or continuous function. In particular, if u,vu,vu,v have prescribed rows and D[u]=D[v]D[u]=D[v]D[u]=D[v], then D((u−v)D[b])=0.D\bigl((u-v)D[b]\bigr)=0.D((u−v)D[b])=0.

Status: DIRECT_COROLLARY of smooth Leibniz, fixed-measure dominated convergence, and the prescribed-row coefficient control. No joint BT convergence is needed.

Proof. For a smooth row member uju_juj​, separate closedness and smooth Leibniz give D(ujD[b])=Duj∧D[b]=D(bDuj).D\bigl(u_jD[b]\bigr)=Du_j\wedge D[b] =D\bigl(bDu_j\bigr).D(uj​D[b])=Duj​∧D[b]=D(bDuj​). For a fixed compact original test, its coefficient measures against D[b]D[b]D[b] are finite signed Radon measures. The row has a common bound near that support and decreases to the actual function uuu. Dominated convergence therefore gives ujD[b]→uD[b]u_jD[b]\to uD[b]uj​D[b]→uD[b] on the fixed test and on its DDD-derivative. On the other hand D[uj]→D[u]D[u_j]\to D[u]D[uj​]→D[u] distributionally. Positivity and the coefficient control permit multiplication of this convergence by the fixed continuous function bbb. Passing to the limit proves the first identity. Subtract the corresponding identity for vvv to obtain the last assertion. ◻

A bounded continuous potential for a nonrigid parameter point

Lemma (Full-fiber integration is continuous in the parameter). Let FFF be complete, let ZZZ be a good Hausdorff boundaryless smooth FFF-analytic space of pure dimension nnn, and let AAA be an ordinary open in AF1,an\mathbf A_F^{1,\rm an}AF1,an​. For an original compact smooth (n,n)(n,n)(n,n)-form η\etaη on Z×FAZ\times_F AZ×F​A, put Iη(a)=∫ZH(a)ηa.I_\eta(a)=\int_{Z_{\mathscr H(a)}}\eta_a.Iη​(a)=∫ZH(a)​​ηa​. Then IηI_\etaIη​ is an ordinary continuous function on AAA. The fiber is the whole completed-residue-field analytic fiber and its integration uses that field’s original calibration.

Status: EXTERNAL_KNOWN in the stated product setting.

Proof. The projection is separated, flat, boundaryless and purely of relative dimension nnn. The compact support is in particular relatively compact over AAA. The assertion follows from [CLD25, Theorem 16.3.3(d), pp. 447–450], whose conclusion is that IηI_\etaIη​ is GGG-tropically C∞C^\inftyC∞. For clarity about the ordinary topology, on an affinoid neighborhood of a base point a finite compact analytic GGG-cover represents such a function by continuous functions of finitely many unit norms. These representatives agree on intersections. Finite closed-set pasting on that neighborhood gives ordinary continuity. This argument concerns a smooth unweighted form; no continuity of an integral with a discontinuous psh multiplier is asserted here. ◻

Proposition (A continuous full-fiber potential at every nonrigid point). Let CCC be an algebraically closed complete non-Archimedean field, and let a∈AC1,ana\in\mathbf A_C^{1,\rm an}a∈AC1,an​ be a point other than a CCC-rational point. There is a finite continuous function bab_aba​ on AC1,an\mathbf A_C^{1,\rm an}AC1,an​, locally bounded, such that for every ZZZ as in Lemma “Full-fiber integration is continuous in the parameter”,

D[ba∘p]=ja∗[1]ZH(a)D[b_a\circ p]=j_{a*}[1]_{Z_{\mathscr H(a)}}D[ba​∘p]=ja∗​[1]ZH(a)​​

on all original tests of Z×CAC1,anZ\times_C\mathbf A_C^{1,\rm an}Z×C​AC1,an​. The right-hand side denotes the full analytic fiber, with coefficient one. In particular the left-hand side is original-positive and separately closed. The equality remains valid after multiplication by any fixed locally bounded Borel function on the product.

The type-IV passage uses a uniform potential limit and unweighted fiber-integral continuity. The limiting construction is included because using the full fiber, and only then adding a fixed Borel multiplier, is essential in the subsequent kernel argument.

Proof. Over CCC, the classification of points of the affine line says that a type-II or type-III point is ζc,r\zeta_{c,r}ζc,r​ with c∈Cc\in Cc∈C and r>0r>0r>0. In that case take ba(t)=log⁡max⁡(r,∣t−c∣).b_a(t)=\log\max(r,|t-c|).ba​(t)=logmax(r,∣t−c∣). Spreading and algebraic closure with prescribed tests

Lemma (Spreading over an auxiliary complete field). Let FFF be complete, let XXX be an ordinary open in a smooth affine FFF-variety, and let a∈AF1,ana\in\mathbf A_F^{1,\rm an}a∈AF1,an​. Every original compact test β\betaβ on XH(a)X_{\mathscr H(a)}XH(a)​ is exactly the restriction of an original compact test α\alphaα on X×FAX\times_F AX×F​A for some ordinary neighborhood AAA of aaa. The equality commutes with DDD.

Proof. The affine-case proof of Lemma R4–77.2 uses only affinoid density and original smooth cutoffs, and works over the present FFF. Its essential steps can be stated directly. On finitely many compact rational norm boxes, replace the analytic unit moments of β\betaβ by rational moments with the same norms, using errors smaller than their positive minimum norms. Localize with norm profiles constant below a positive threshold at every possible zero; impose separate lower cutoffs on the unit moments. There are then finitely many coefficients in H(a)\mathscr H(a)H(a). Approximate them by values of rational functions in F(t)F(t)F(t) with denominators nonzero at aaa. Such values are dense by the definition of the completed residue field. Uniform coefficient bounds on a fixed compact affine stage preserve exactly every active unit norm, and preserve every zero-protected profile on the whole stage. Thus the localized forms remain exactly equal on the fiber. Remove the finite denominator zero loci in an ordinary parameter neighborhood and add compact cutoffs in XXX and in that neighborhood. Their supports lie in a finite union of compact analytic products of affinoid domains. This gives α\alphaα with the stated exact restriction. All operations were constructions of smooth test forms, with no psh regularization over FFF. ◻

Now take an original compact test β\betaβ on XCX_CXC​. Rationalize and localize its finitely many unit moments as in the preceding lemma. Only finitely many coefficients in CCC remain. Approximate all of them by elements of FalgF^{\rm alg}Falg, with errors below all the fixed unit and profile thresholds. They lie in a common finite extension F′/FF'/FF′/F. The resulting compact F′F'F′-test η\etaη pulls back to exactly β\betaβ: active logarithms and zero-protected profiles, hence the differential forms, are unchanged. This theorem closes the scalar-extension gate isolated in R4. It does not by itself prove continuity of the actual difference u−vu-vu−v, or its functoriality under every analytic map over an arbitrary extension. Those are separate assertions. In particular the arbitrary-background quotient is not invoked anywhere in the proof and is not claimed as a consequence without the remaining analytic argument.

Analytic pullback of the bounded kernel after every complete extension

The ground field of the original potentials is the fixed finite extension K/QpK/\mathbf Q_pK/Qp​, with its original absolute value. An allowed space over a complete extension L/KL/KL/K is good, Hausdorff, boundaryless, and quasi-smooth. In particular, its structural morphism is smooth in the sense of Berkovich. We use the original CLD forms and currents over the indicated field. The functions are actual locally bounded classical psh functions, with the all-complete-extension curve condition.

The result of this section is a pullback statement for differences of specified functions. No pullback of an arbitrary current is defined. Algebraic neighborhoods and tubular neighborhoods are used only over the original finite field KKK, where B, Lemma D.4, and R, Lemma 5.2, supply them. The new source over LLL is handled by genuinely etale coordinates and a field-independent normal trace.

Lemma (Ordinary finite etale coordinates). Let LLL be a complete nontrivially valued field and let ZZZ be a good, boundaryless, quasi-smooth LLL-analytic space. For every point z∈Zz\in Zz∈Z of local dimension ddd, there are ordinary open neighborhoods Z0Z_0Z0​ of zzz and BBB in ALd,an\mathbf A_L^{d,\mathrm{an}}ALd,an​ and a finite etale morphism g:Z0⟶B.g:Z_0\longrightarrow B.g:Z0​⟶B. The neighborhoods can be made small enough to meet any prescribed ordinary neighborhood condition at zzz.

Status: EXTERNAL_KNOWN. The precise geometry is the definition of smooth morphisms in Berkovich [Ber93, §3.5], together with the definition of quasifinite morphisms in [Ber93, Definition 3.1.1 and Lemma 3.1.2] and the fact that etale morphisms are quasifinite in [Ber93, 3.3.4]. These conventions and their ordinary-open meaning are also stated explicitly on printed page 9 of that paper.

Proof. Smoothness gives, after an ordinary shrinking at zzz, an etale map to ALd,an\mathbf A_L^{d,\mathrm{an}}ALd,an​. In Berkovich’s terminology an etale map is quasifinite. Quasifiniteness means that at the chosen source point it restricts to a finite map between ordinary open neighborhoods of that point and its image. The restriction remains etale. Starting with the prescribed smaller ordinary neighborhood proves the final assertion. This argument does not replace etale by quasi-etale: an analytic-domain immersion with relative boundary would not justify the assertion. Boundarylessness in the hypotheses is used precisely to pass from quasi-smoothness to smoothness. ◻

WL×LALd,an.W_L\times_L\mathbf A_L^{d,\mathrm{an}}.WL​×L​ALd,an​.

The actual harmonic representative on complete-extension curves

The distinction between equality of curve distributions and equality of actual functions matters here. Thuillier’s degree-zero distributions are determined by the values at points of type II or III. An arbitrary Borel modification at a rigid point would not be detected by those values. The following argument recovers the missing values from the separate subharmonicity of the two given functions. It does not assume that their difference is semicontinuous.

Lemma (The algebraic scope of the curve input). Over any complete nontrivially valued field FFF, a good Hausdorff boundaryless quasi-smooth analytic curve is, locally for the ordinary topology, isomorphic to an ordinary open in the analytification of a smooth affine algebraic FFF-curve. No extension of FFF is necessary. Consequently the explicitly complete-field statement of B, Lemma A.2, applies locally to actual locally bounded subharmonic functions on such an analytic curve, when char⁡F=0\operatorname{char}F=0charF=0.

A boundary of this conclusion.

The theorem establishes actual continuity and harmonicity on each of the permitted source curves, after all complete extensions. It does not replace a proof of ordinary continuity of u−vu-vu−v on the higher-dimensional target. In the definition of classical pluriharmonicity that additional topological condition still has to be established; no such inference is made from density of curve images alone.

A Shilov maximum principle without ambient upper semicontinuity

Throughout this section the absolute values are fixed, and scalar extensions carry the extending absolute value. Harmonicity on a smooth analytic curve means harmonicity of the actual function; in particular that function is continuous on the curve. We do not assume that a function which has harmonic curve pullbacks is upper semicontinuous on its higher-dimensional ambient space.

Scope and use of the ambient neighborhood.

The regularity of the gig_igi​ on YYY ensures that every sliced affinoid curve is contained in the analytification of an algebraic curve extending across its compact boundary. Merely knowing a harmonic function on the interior of an abstract affinoid curve would not justify its boundary maximum with arbitrary assigned boundary values. The theorem states the needed ambient condition explicitly. It requires no global psh exhaustion and no strictly positive ambient form. Producing the indicated affinoids and ambient regular normalization coordinates is a separate geometric input; it is not inferred from the maximum principle itself.

Proof. First, R∧R^\wedgeR∧ is a Noetherian regular ring. Here is a reduction to local completion, avoiding an unstated formal-model normality assumption. Every maximal ideal n\mathfrak nn of R∧R^\wedgeR∧ contains ϖ\varpiϖ: for every b∈R∧b\in R^\wedgeb∈R∧, the geometric series makes 1−ϖb1-\varpi b1−ϖb invertible. Put m=n∩R\mathfrak m=\mathfrak n\cap Rm=n∩R. Since R∧/ϖR∧=R/ϖRR^\wedge/\varpi R^\wedge=R/\varpi RR∧/ϖR∧=R/ϖR, this is a maximal ideal and n=mR∧\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mR^\wedgen=mR∧. The local map Rm⟶(R∧)nR_{\mathfrak m}\longrightarrow (R^\wedge)_{\mathfrak n}Rm​⟶(R∧)n​ is flat, has the same residue field, and extends the maximal ideal to the maximal ideal. It therefore induces an isomorphism of maximal-ideal completions [Stacks, Tag 0AGX]. Regularity is equivalent to regularity of that completion [Stacks, Tag 07NY]. Thus every maximal localization of R∧R^\wedgeR∧ is regular, and so is R∧R^\wedgeR∧.

The ring R∧R^\wedgeR∧ is normal. It is also connected: any idempotent reduces to 000 or 111 modulo ϖ\varpiϖ because R/ϖRR/\varpi RR/ϖR is connected, and that reduction determines the idempotent in the complete ring. A connected Noetherian normal ring is a domain. Flatness of completion preserves the fact that ϖ\varpiϖ is a nonzero divisor. The height-one primes containing ϖ\varpiϖ are exactly the generic points of the components of R∧/ϖR∧=R/ϖRR^\wedge/\varpi R^\wedge=R/\varpi RR∧/ϖR∧=R/ϖR. Lemma (Small algebraic charts with logarithmic interpolation). Let N\mathcal NN be a strictly semistable finite-type F∘F^\circF∘-scheme in the sense of de Jong [dJ96, §2.16]: it is regular and flat, and its special fiber is a reduced strict normal crossings divisor. Let s∈Nss\in\mathcal N_ss∈Ns​. There is an algebraic affine neighborhood U=Spec⁡R\mathcal U=\operatorname{Spec}RU=SpecR of sss with the following properties. Its nonempty special fiber is reduced and connected, with irreducible components D0,…,DrD_0,\ldots,D_rD0​,…,Dr​ all containing sss. There are regular functions x0,…,xrx_0,\ldots,x_rx0​,…,xr​ defining these components as effective Cartier divisors and satisfying x0⋯xr=ϖx_0\cdots x_r=\varpix0​⋯xr​=ϖ. Its formal generic fiber WWW is a strict affinoid domain in the smooth algebraic generic fiber UFan\mathcal U_F^{\rm an}UFan​, and its Shilov boundary is the set {ξ0,…,ξr}\{\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_r\}{ξ0​,…,ξr​} in Lemma “Vertical components are the exact Shilov boundary”.

For any prescribed real numbers c0,…,crc_0,\ldots,c_rc0​,…,cr​, the function

h=−1−log⁡∣ϖ∣∑i=0rcilog⁡∣xi∣h=-\frac{1}{-\log|\varpi|} \sum_{i=0}^r c_i\log|x_i|h=−−log∣ϖ∣1​i=0∑r​ci​log∣xi​∣

is continuous on the whole algebraic generic fiber, is harmonic after every pullback to a smooth analytic curve over every complete extension, and satisfies h(ξi)=cih(\xi_i)=c_ih(ξi​)=ci​. Every topological affinoid generator of WWW can be chosen as the restriction of a regular function on UF\mathcal U_FUF​.

Status: DIRECT_COROLLARY of the strictly semistable divisor description and the preceding lemma. No algebraic closure or splitting of all strata is needed.

Proof. Strict semistability implies regularity of N\mathcal NN, reducedness of its special fiber, and that each irreducible component of the special fiber is an effective Cartier divisor; these are the properties in [dJ96, §2.16]. Remove all special-fiber components not containing sss. Shrink to an algebraic affine neighborhood of sss on which the remaining finitely many Cartier divisors are principal, say with equations xix_ixi​. Their restrictions remain irreducible: each is a nonempty Zariski-open subset of its original irreducible component. They all meet at sss, so their union is connected. The ambient regular scheme can be restricted to its component containing sss, giving the integral ring RRR.

The effective Cartier divisor of ϖ\varpiϖ is exactly D0+⋯+DrD_0+\cdots+D_rD0​+⋯+Dr​, each with coefficient one. Therefore x0⋯xr/ϖx_0\cdots x_r/\varpix0​⋯xr​/ϖ is a regular unit after a further shrinking around sss. Absorb its inverse into x0x_0x0​ to obtain the stated product equality. Each xix_ixi​ is a unit on UF\mathcal U_FUF​.

Apply Lemma “Vertical components are the exact Shilov boundary”. Its coordinate values give h(ξi)=cih(\xi_i)=c_ih(ξi​)=ci​. The function hhh is a real linear combination of logarithms of analytic units on a genuine boundaryless algebraic neighborhood of WWW. Such logarithms are continuous and have harmonic curve pullbacks, also after arbitrary complete scalar extension. Finally, finite-type algebraic generators of RRR give topological generators after completion and inverting ϖ\varpiϖ, and are regular on UF\mathcal U_FUF​. ◻

Use in the continuity argument.

For an actual curvewise harmonic function fff, choose ci=f(ξi)c_i=f(\xi_i)ci​=f(ξi​). If the separately proved Shilov principle applies on WWW with its ambient regular Noether coordinates, then it applies to f−hf-hf−h. The latter vanishes on every Shilov point, and hence f=hf=hf=h everywhere on WWW. This deduction uses no ambient semicontinuity of fff and no pre-existing pluriharmonicity of fff.

Algebraic neighborhoods for the continuity argument

This section isolates the geometry needed for a Shilov maximum argument. The original field is a fixed finite extension K/QpK/\mathbf Q_pK/Qp​, with its given absolute value. No function in this section is assumed upper semicontinuous merely because its restrictions to curves are harmonic.

Lemma (Polynomial Noether coordinates). Let FFF be a complete nontrivially valued field of characteristic zero. Let YYY be a smooth affine FFF-variety of pure dimension nnn, and let V⊂YanV\subset Y^{\mathrm{an}}V⊂Yan be a strictly affinoid domain. Assume that the affinoid algebra A=O(V)A=\mathscr O(V)A=O(V) has a finite Tate presentation A=F⟨T1,…,Tm⟩/IA=F\langle T_1,\ldots,T_m\rangle/IA=F⟨T1​,…,Tm​⟩/I whose generators a1,…,ama_1,\ldots,a_ma1​,…,am​ are restrictions of regular functions on YYY. Then there are polynomials P1,…,Pn∈F[T1,…,Tm]P_1,\ldots,P_n\in F[T_1,\ldots,T_m]P1​,…,Pn​∈F[T1​,…,Tm​] for which gi=Pi(a1,…,am),F⟨Z1,…,Zn⟩⟶A,Zi↦gi,g_i=P_i(a_1,\ldots,a_m),\qquad F\langle Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\rangle\longrightarrow A,\quad Z_i\mapsto g_i,gi​=Pi​(a1​,…,am​),F⟨Z1​,…,Zn​⟩⟶A,Zi​↦gi​, is finite and faithfully flat. Thus g=(g1,…,gn)g=(g_1,\ldots,g_n)g=(g1​,…,gn​) gives a finite flat surjection V→BFnV\to\mathbb B_F^nV→BFn​, and each gig_igi​ extends regularly to the boundaryless algebraic ambient space.

Status: DIRECT_COROLLARY of polynomial Noether normalization and miracle flatness. The extension of the coordinates is part of the conclusion; it is not an assumed extension theorem for arbitrary affinoid functions.

Proof. Write A=F⟨T1,…,Tm⟩/IA=F\langle T_1,\ldots,T_m\rangle/IA=F⟨T1​,…,Tm​⟩/I using the given tuple. The proof of affinoid Noether normalization uses triangular polynomial automorphisms Ti⟼Ti+TmNi(i<m),Tm⟼Tm,T_i\longmapsto T_i+T_m^{N_i}\quad(i<m),\qquad T_m\longmapsto T_m,Ti​⟼Ti​+TmNi​​(i<m),Tm​⟼Tm​, their polynomial inverses, and coordinate inclusions. One chooses a nonzero element of the current ideal, makes it distinguished in the last variable, and uses Weierstrass division to obtain a finite map from the algebra in one fewer variables. Induction on mmm gives an injective finite map from a Tate algebra of dimension dim⁡A=n\dim A=ndimA=n. Since every change of variables is polynomial, the images of its variables are polynomials in the original tuple. This is the construction in Bosch’s April 2008 manuscript, §1.2, Lemma 7 and Corollary 10, printed pages 11 and 14 [Bosch08]. It does not replace the given tuple by arbitrary analytic functions on VVV.

The algebra AAA is regular and of pure dimension nnn, since VVV is an analytic domain in the smooth YanY^{\mathrm{an}}Yan. At a maximal ideal of the Tate algebra, its local ring is regular of dimension nnn. Every maximal localization of the finite algebra above it is Cohen–Macaulay of dimension nnn, and its fiber is zero dimensional. Miracle flatness, in the form of [Stacks, Tag 00R4], gives flatness at these localizations. A finite module is flat if and only if its localizations at maximal ideals are flat, so the map is finite flat. Its injection and integrality make the map on spectra, hence the finite map of affinoid spaces, surjective. The regular extension of gig_igi​ is the displayed polynomial expression. ◻

Lemma (Algebraic norm boxes). Let YYY be a smooth affine KKK-variety and let UUU be an ordinary open in YanY^{\mathrm{an}}Yan. Every x∈Ux\in Ux∈U has a strictly affinoid neighborhood V⊂UV\subset UV⊂U which is the generic fiber of the π\piπ-adic completion of an integral affine finite-type flat K∘K^\circK∘-scheme M\mathcal MM, after restricting to one irreducible component at xxx. Its algebraic generic fiber is an affine Zariski open Y0⊂YY_0\subset YY0​⊂Y, and O(V)\mathscr O(V)O(V) admits a finite Tate-presentation generating tuple whose entries are restrictions of regular functions on Y0Y_0Y0​. The point xxx is in the ordinary interior of VVV.

Proof. Use the topology of the analytification of an affine variety: absolute values of finitely many regular functions give basic ordinary neighborhoods. Choose strict upper and, where needed, strict positive lower bounds at xxx, within the prescribed neighborhood. The bounds can be chosen in ∣K×∣Q|K^\times|^{\mathbf Q}∣K×∣Q, since its logarithm is a dense subgroup of R\mathbf RR. Add sufficiently loose upper bounds for a finite set of affine coordinates to make the closed box compact. Replacing the bounds by non-strict inequalities gives an affinoid neighborhood still contained in UUU; the strict inequalities at xxx ensure that xxx is an interior point.

After inverting the functions with positive lower bounds, we are on an affine Zariski open Y0Y_0Y0​. Raising a defining inequality to a positive integral power and multiplying by an integral power of π\piπ writes it as ∣ai∣≤1|a_i|\leq1∣ai​∣≤1, with aia_iai​ regular on Y0Y_0Y0​. Add a scaled finite generating set of K[Y0]K[Y_0]K[Y0​] whose norms are at most one on the box. These additional inequalities do not alter the box. Put M0=K∘[a1,…,am]⊂K[Y0].M_0=K^\circ[a_1,\ldots,a_m]\subset K[Y_0].M0​=K∘[a1​,…,am​]⊂K[Y0​]. Then M0[1/π]=K[Y0]M_0[1/\pi]=K[Y_0]M0​[1/π]=K[Y0​] and M0M_0M0​ is a finite-type, torsion-free K∘K^\circK∘-algebra. It is flat over the DVR K∘K^\circK∘. Its π\piπ-adic completion has generic fiber the affinoid domain defined by the chosen inequalities: the universal affinoid presentation adjoins precisely the displayed power-bounded generators. Thus M=Spec⁡M0\mathcal M=\operatorname{Spec}M_0M=SpecM0​ has the required properties. Smooth components of YYY are disjoint locally; restrict to the component containing xxx to obtain integrality. This construction uses the original absolute value and makes no normalization ∣π∣=e−1|\pi|=e^{-1}∣π∣=e−1. ◻

Each chart has regular functions x0,…,xrx_0,\ldots,x_rx0​,…,xr​ defining the irreducible components of its reduced special fiber, with x0⋯xr=ϖx_0\cdots x_r=\varpix0​⋯xr​=ϖ for a uniformizer ϖ\varpiϖ of K′K'K′. The continuous logarithmic functions λi=−log⁡∣xi∣−log⁡∣ϖ∣,∑i=0rλi=1\lambda_i=-\frac{\log|x_i|}{-\log|\varpi|},\qquad \sum_{i=0}^r\lambda_i=1λi​=−−log∣ϖ∣log∣xi​∣​,i=0∑r​λi​=1 satisfy λi(ξj)=δij\lambda_i(\xi_j)=\delta_{ij}λi​(ξj​)=δij​. In particular, the compact charts occur inside actual ordinary ambient neighborhoods. They are not treated as boundaryless merely because they have formal models.

Status: DIRECT_COROLLARY of de Jong’s Theorem 6.5 [dJ96] and Lemma “Small algebraic charts with logarithmic interpolation”. Strict semistability here has de Jong’s meaning: the total scheme is regular and its special fiber is a reduced strict normal-crossing divisor. No assertion about an entire skeleton is needed.

Proof. Apply [dJ96, Theorem 6.5] to M\mathcal MM and its special fiber. It gives a finite extension of traits Spec⁡K′∘→Spec⁡K∘\operatorname{Spec}K'^\circ\to\operatorname{Spec}K^\circSpecK′∘→SpecK∘, an alteration N→M\mathcal N\to\mathcal MN→M, and an open embedding of N\mathcal NN in a projective strictly semistable scheme. Thus N\mathcal NN itself is strictly semistable and is proper over M\mathcal MM. Its generic fiber ZZZ is smooth over K′K'K′ and has an algebraic proper surjection to Y0Y_0Y0​.

Let WWW be the generic fiber of the completion of N\mathcal NN along its special fiber. It is exactly the inverse image of VVV in ZanZ^{\mathrm{an}}Zan. To check this at an actual point zzz, the condition that its image belong to VVV says that the corresponding map to M\mathcal MM extends over H(z)∘\mathscr H(z)^\circH(z)∘. The valuative criterion for the proper map N→M\mathcal N\to\mathcal MN→M uniquely extends the map to N\mathcal NN. Its center belongs to the special fiber, which is exactly the condition z∈Wz\in Wz∈W. The reverse inclusion follows directly from the morphism of completions. The analytic map W→VW\to VW→V is proper and surjective and WWW is compact.

Apply Lemma “Small algebraic charts with logarithmic interpolation” at every point of the special fiber of N\mathcal NN. Quasicompactness gives finitely many of its small algebraic affine charts. Completing them gives the asserted finite affinoid cover. Their finite-type coordinate rings supply regular topological generators on their algebraic generic fibers. The lemma gives the exact Shilov boundary and the logarithmic coordinate values over the same field K′K'K′. In particular no algebraic closure or splitting of strata is involved. Every chart maps into VVV, while its ordinary algebraic neighborhood maps into UUU after restricting to the inverse image of UUU. This proves the ambient assertion. ◻

Theorem (Continuity from actual curvewise harmonicity). Let f:U→Rf:U\to\mathbf Rf:U→R be an actual real-valued function on an allowed KKK-analytic space. Suppose that after every complete extension F/KF/KF/K, its pullback along every analytic map from an ordinary open in a smooth algebraic FFF-curve is an actual continuous harmonic function. Then fff is continuous and therefore locally bounded.

Status: NEW_PROVED, using Theorem “Curvewise harmonic functions satisfy the affinoid Shilov bound”. No semicontinuity, local boundedness, or Borel measurability of fff is among the assumptions. Finiteness of its actual values and actual harmonicity on the indicated curves are essential.

Proof. Zero-dimensional smooth spaces are locally discrete, and their case is immediate. In positive dimension, B, Lemma D.4, allows us to work in an ordinary open of a smooth affine KKK-variety. Around a given point choose a norm box V⋐UV\Subset UV⋐U with that point in its ordinary interior. Use Proposition “Semistable covers with an algebraic ambient map”. For a chart WλW_\lambdaWλ​, denote its Shilov points by ξ0,…,ξr\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_rξ0​,…,ξr​ and put hλ=∑i=0r(f∘q)(ξi)λi.h_\lambda=\sum_{i=0}^r(f\circ q)(\xi_i)\lambda_i .hλ​=i=0∑r​(f∘q)(ξi​)λi​. This is continuous. It is a real linear combination of logarithms of analytic units, so its pullback to every smooth curve is harmonic. The same is true of f∘q−hλf\circ q-h_\lambdaf∘q−hλ​ by the assumed curve property of fff. The difference vanishes on every Shilov point of WλW_\lambdaWλ​.

The affinoid generators of WλW_\lambdaWλ​ extend to its smooth algebraic neighborhood. Lemma “Polynomial Noether coordinates” therefore gives finite flat Noether coordinates extending to that neighborhood. Apply Theorem “Curvewise harmonic functions satisfy the affinoid Shilov bound” over K′K'K′ to the difference. Its absolute value is bounded by its maximum on the Shilov boundary, which is zero. Hence f∘q=hλon Wλ.f\circ q=h_\lambda \quad\hbox{on }W_\lambda.f∘q=hλ​on Wλ​. The finitely many affinoid domains WλW_\lambdaWλ​ are compact, hence closed in the Hausdorff compact space WWW. Closed-set pasting shows that f∘qf\circ qf∘q is continuous on WWW. Finally a continuous surjection from a compact space onto the Hausdorff space VVV is a quotient map. Since f∘qf\circ qf∘q is constant on its fibers by its definition, f∣Vf|_Vf∣V​ is continuous. The ordinary interiors of these VVV cover UUU, proving the claim. ◻

Logical boundary.

This argument has not used upper semicontinuous regularization of fff, convergence of moving coefficient measures, pullback of an arbitrary current, or a strictly psh exhaustion of every analytic domain. Its indispensable analytic input is the Shilov principle for the actual curvewise harmonic function on compact slices with boundaryless ambient neighborhoods.

The arbitrary-background potential quotient

Fix a finite extension K/QpK/\mathbf Q_pK/Qp​ with its original absolute value. Let UUU be an ordinary open in a good Hausdorff boundaryless quasi-smooth KKK-analytic space of pure dimension nnn. Throughout this section D=d′d′′D=d'd''D=d′d′′, the test forms are all original compactly supported CLD smooth complementary forms, and positivity is the original positive cone used in R. Every positive current under consideration is symmetric. Strong and weak positivity are not substituted for that cone.

Write DSHlb(U)\mathscr{DSH}_{\mathrm{lb}}(U)DSHlb​(U) for the actual real functions which are locally differences of two members of Cb\mathcal C_bCb​. A function in PH(U)\mathscr{PH}(U)PH(U) is a finite continuous function whose two signs are classical psh. Such a function is locally bounded. No quotient by a measure-null set occurs in either definition.

Theorem (Regularity of the bounded classical curvature kernel). If u,v∈Cb(U)u,v\in\mathcal C_b(U)u,v∈Cb​(U) and D[u]=D[v]D[u]=D[v]D[u]=D[v] on every original test, then the actual difference u−vu-vu−v is continuous and belongs to PH(U)\mathscr{PH}(U)PH(U). More generally, ker⁡(D:DSHlb(U)⟶D′1,1(U))=PH(U).\ker\bigl(D:\mathscr{DSH}_{\mathrm{lb}}(U) \longrightarrow\mathcal D'^{1,1}(U)\bigr) =\mathscr{PH}(U).ker(D:DSHlb​(U)⟶D′1,1(U))=PH(U). The equality is an equality of spaces of actual functions. It does not assert regularity for the kernel on all locally integrable functions or on all abstract distributions.

Status: NEW_PROVED in the stated bounded-classical scope, relative to the declared internal inputs and the preceding proofs.

Proof. Let H=u−vH=u-vH=u−v. Theorem “Actual harmonicity on every complete-extension curve” shows that after every complete extension F/KF/KF/K, the pullback of HHH along every allowed smooth analytic curve is an actual continuous harmonic function. In particular it has the algebraic-curve property required by Theorem “Continuity from actual curvewise harmonicity”. That theorem applies to the actual locally bounded HHH and proves its ordinary continuity on UUU.

Both HHH and −H-H−H are therefore upper semicontinuous. To check the full curve quantifier, let C→UFC\to U_FC→UF​ be an arbitrary FFF-analytic curve map, including curves with boundary or singularities. Its two pullbacks are continuous. In the definition of subharmonicity on CCC, test further over any complete extension E/FE/FE/F by a smooth connected strict EEE-curve mapping to CEC_ECE​. Smooth curves can be localized in good Hausdorff boundaryless ordinary opens, and subharmonicity is local. Definition 3.4 and §4.1.3 of [GR25] therefore give subharmonicity on the original CCC. Undifferentiated weights and limits.

The quotient is for differentiated slots. An undifferentiated weight is still an actual function: replacing it by another function with the same curvature need not preserve a weighted current. The seven established fixed-background BT properties retain their original functional hypotheses. This section does not turn arbitrary weak convergence of curvature currents or arbitrary varying backgrounds into weighted joint convergence.

Original tests and the remaining boundaries of scope.

The operation above is an equality of ordinary original CLD currents. It is not promoted to equality on all delta-test forms. It does not define the wedge of two completely arbitrary positive closed currents. An arbitrary permitted SSS may still charge an ambient pluripolar set. Neither the regularity theorem nor the quotient proof requires that such concentration be excluded.

Positivity and scope.

If every differentiated slot admits a classical psh local potential, the operation agrees with the already positive BT product. For the general signed class above, positivity is not part of the assertion. In particular, this section does not claim that a positive current of the form D[H]D[H]D[H] with a bounded classical difference potential necessarily has a classical psh potential. It does not claim that all positive closed currents, or all signed closed currents, belong to Vcl1,1\mathscr V^{1,1}_{\mathrm{cl}}Vcl1,1​.

There is one arbitrary positive separately closed background and finitely many differentiated local-potential slots. No product of two entirely arbitrary currents is defined. The construction is an equality of original ordinary CLD currents, with no promotion to all delta-test forms or to the general nonclosed, nonpositive, off-diagonal GK calculus.

Exact boundary of the conclusion.

The background over LLL is unrestricted within the stated positive separately closed class. The potentials, however, are induced from bounded classical potentials over the original KKK. The descent hypothesis is equality of the original KKK-curvatures; no assertion is made for additional equalities arising only after pullback over LLL. Neither result asserts regularization, kernel regularity, full slot symmetry, or joint monotone BT continuity for all unknown bounded classical functions over LLL. No pullback of SSS, or of a mixed current with arbitrary background, is defined. All equalities remain ordinary original-current equalities rather than equalities on every delta-test form.

Provenance and limits of the consequence.

The preceding argument is the finite-dimensional Shilov argument of [GR25, Proposition 7.3 and Theorems 7.4–7.6], applied after the new identification of the actual original-current kernel. The proof of its Theorem 7.6 already contains the finite-evaluation mechanism; here it is written for nets and with continuity of the finite pointwise limit derived explicitly. No novelty is claimed for that elementary consequence. The finite dimension is asserted on a fixed quasicompact domain or for restrictions to a fixed compact affinoid cover. It does not assert a uniform bound for dimensions as neighborhoods shrink, or a finite-dimensional stalk of the pluriharmonic sheaf.

Exact vanishing D[Hi]=0D[H_i]=0D[Hi​]=0 is essential to this statement. Weak convergence D[Hi]→0D[H_i]\to0D[Hi​]→0 alone does not imply it, even for uniformly bounded continuous classical difference presentations: Example “Uniform bounded psh decompositions and universal strong energy do not suffice” has a nonzero actual polar-carried limit and a persistent relative curvature defect. Thus this corollary does not replace any capacitary or weighted convergence hypothesis by weak curvature convergence.

What the criterion does and does not require.

All the degree-one backgrounds are fixed smooth wedges of the one given SSS; there is no sequence of backgrounds. The positive square spanning family accounts for every original complementary test, including tests with new moment coordinates. The criterion requires energy of the error, after an actual pluriharmonic correction, to tend to zero. Strong energy convergence to a different assigned Borel representative does not satisfy this requirement. In particular it does not rescue the weak-current or completed-polar-selector failures recorded earlier. No assertion about varying mixed BT tails or joint higher mixed-current convergence follows from this first-order estimate alone.

A finite-field check for normal Gauss coarea

This section checks a possible failure mode in the normal trace: could a finite residue-field extension split after adjoining the normal Gauss parameter, or create extra correlated points on the calibrated support? The answer for this particular product support is no. The following finite-dimensional argument requires neither stability of the valued field nor a ramification–residue-degree formula.

Lemma (Finite extensions commute with Gauss completion). Let FFF be a complete non-Archimedean field, let E/FE/FE/F be a finite valued extension with its extending absolute value, and let r>0r>0r>0 be any real radius. Denote by FrF_rFr​ the completion of F(T)F(T)F(T) for the radius-rrr Gauss norm and by ErE_rEr​ the analogous completion of E(T)E(T)E(T). Then the natural homomorphism

E⊗FFr⟶ErE\otimes_F F_r\longrightarrow E_rE⊗F​Fr​⟶Er​

is an isomorphism of finite FrF_rFr​-algebras. In particular, its source is a field and [Er:Fr]=[E:F].[E_r:F_r]=[E:F].[Er​:Fr​]=[E:F]. There is only one point in the Berkovich spectrum of this finite FrF_rFr​-algebra, with the full displayed algebraic degree. No rationality assumption on rrr is imposed.

Status: DIRECT_COROLLARY of finite-dimensional norm equivalence and the Gauss norm. The proof is given because it is exactly the field assertion needed in the product calibration, including in the presence of defect.

The span of the first d−1d-1d−1 vectors is complete by the induction hypothesis, hence closed in EEE. Its distance from ede_ded​ is positive. Consequently the norm of ∑ieiai\sum_i e_i a_i∑i​ei​ai​ controls ∣ad∣|a_d|∣ad​∣; the ultrametric triangle inequality then controls the norm of the first d−1d-1d−1 summands, and induction controls their coefficients. The upper estimate is the triangle inequality. This proves (eq:r5-finite-basis-norm-equivalence) without an orthogonal-basis assertion.

For polynomials Pi(T)∈F[T]P_i(T)\in F[T]Pi​(T)∈F[T], apply (eq:r5-finite-basis-norm-equivalence) separately to every coefficient and then take the weighted maximum over the powers of TTT. The result is

cmax⁡i∥Pi∥r≤∥∑ieiPi∥r≤Cmax⁡i∥Pi∥r.c\max_i\|P_i\|_r \leq\left\|\sum_i e_iP_i\right\|_r \leq C\max_i\|P_i\|_r.cimax​∥Pi​∥r​≤​i∑​ei​Pi​​r​≤Cimax​∥Pi​∥r​.

The same inequalities hold for Pi∈F(T)P_i\in F(T)Pi​∈F(T) after clearing one common denominator in F[T]F[T]F[T] and dividing by its nonzero Gauss norm.

Algebraically E⊗FF(T)=E(T)E\otimes_F F(T)=E(T)E⊗F​F(T)=E(T), and the same eie_iei​ form an F(T)F(T)F(T)-basis. To see explicitly that a denominator in E[T]E[T]E[T] causes no problem, multiplication by such a nonzero polynomial is injective on the free F[T]F[T]F[T]-module E[T]E[T]E[T]. After localizing F[T]F[T]F[T], it is an injective endomorphism of a finite-dimensional F(T)F(T)F(T)-space, hence is invertible. The full fiber of the projection to the normal parameter may contain correlated points, such as those on which ∣x−T∣|x-T|∣x−T∣ is smaller than both ∣x∣|x|∣x∣ and ∣T∣|T|∣T∣. An arbitrary form on the full fiber, involving mixed moments such as x−Tx-Tx−T, need not have this support. This precise distinction is what makes the normal trace compatible with the correlated-point counterexample recorded in R4.

No faithfulness condition on the background.

The final argument for SSS uses that a symmetric original current and its negative cannot both be positive unless they are zero. It does not require the coefficient measures of SSS to detect every point or every ordinary open set. Thus S=0S=0S=0, backgrounds with smaller support, and integration currents carried by ambient pluripolar subvarieties all remain within scope. At p=np=np=n there is no further differentiated degree; the statement is vacuous rather than an additional analytic assertion.

Finite extensions retain the original calibration.

For a finite extension F/KF/KF/K of degree ddd, the integration current of an FFF-space viewed as a KKK-space is ddd times its FFF-calibrated current on common original tests. By contrast, scalar pushforward of the FFF-calibrated top-form measure has factor one. These are respectively the conventions of [CLD25, Remark 14.4.3, p. 410, and Proposition 15.3.1, p. 425]. They are compatible: the finite morphism viewed over KKK has degree ddd. The kernel arguments divide a zero pairing by this single positive factor when necessary; they neither change the absolute value nor introduce a power of ddd for differentiated slots. No ramification–residue-degree identity is required.

The weak-positive current cone is not pointed

We use the terminology of CLD exactly. A symmetric current is weakly positive when it is nonnegative on strongly positive compact tests; it is positive when it is nonnegative on positive compact tests; it is strongly positive when it is nonnegative on weakly positive compact tests. These are [CLD12, Definition 5.4.1] and [CLD25, Definition 7.2.1]. R, Convention 2.2, chooses the middle, original positive cone. The distinction is essential to the two-sign conclusion used in the quotient theorem.

Consequence for the quotient argument.

The original positive cone used by R is pointed on symmetric currents: positive forms span the full symmetric test space, and two opposite positive currents consequently vanish [CLD25, Remark 7.2.3]. Strongly positive tests do not span that space in the example above. Thus replacing “positive” by “weakly positive” in the last two-sign step would be invalid. The construction is not a counterexample to potential independence for weak backgrounds: it supplies neither a nonzero quotient defect nor any pair of potentials with such a defect. It only disproves that proposed proof step and fixes the positivity scope of the present result.

Precise comparison with the printed statements.

As written, [CLD25, Proposition 7.2.9, p. 162] assumes symmetry and nonnegativity on strongly positive tests, and concludes order zero on a locally differentially separated tropical space. The standard space R5\mathbf R^5R5 has that separation property, so Example “Separate closedness does not repair strong-test control” contradicts the order-zero conclusion under its printed hypotheses. The displayed domination step in that proof would require an arbitrary symmetric form α\alphaα to satisfy α+C∥α∥βpstrongly positive\alpha+C\|\alpha\|\beta^p \quad\hbox{strongly positive}α+C∥α∥βpstrongly positive for a fixed positive definite (1,1)(1,1)(1,1)-form β\betaβ. The relative-interior statement in [CLD25, Proposition 1.2.13, pp. 27–28] does not give this: strongly positive forms span only a proper subspace in the middle degrees used here. The same proposition explicitly records this proper-span phenomenon.

There is also a distinct printed strong-span assertion in [CLD12, Lemma 5.3.3, p. 81]: every smooth (p,p)(p,p)(p,p)-form with strongly paracompact support is asserted to be a difference of strongly positive forms. Example “A nonzero smooth closed current in the weak lineality space” disproves that assertion even for symmetric compactly supported original Berkovich forms. Indeed, on the four-dimensional analytic torus take ω=ρ(t)θa+\omega=\rho(t)\theta_{a_+}ω=ρ(t)θa+​​ as in that example. Its compact support meets the stated support hypothesis, and ⟨[γ4],ω⟩>0\langle[\gamma_4],\omega\rangle>0⟨[γ4​],ω⟩>0. If ω=ω1−ω2\omega=\omega_1-\omega_2ω=ω1​−ω2​ with both ωi\omega_iωi​ strongly positive, choose an original nonnegative smooth compact cutoff ξ\xiξ equal to one near supp⁡ω\operatorname{supp}\omegasuppω. Then ω=ξω1−ξω2\omega=\xi\omega_1-\xi\omega_2ω=ξω1​−ξω2​, whereas [γ4][\gamma_4][γ4​] annihilates both compact strongly positive terms. This is a contradiction. The replacement by the middle positive span is the one stated in [CLD25, Proposition 6.5.2]. This analytic strong-span counterexample uses only the smooth original torus current; it does not transport the derivative distribution constructed above.

The earlier [CLD12, Lemma 5.4.4, p. 82] has a different hypothesis: its linear functional is nonnegative on every weakly positive test. Our current does not satisfy that stronger test requirement, so this construction does not refute that lemma. Explicitly, choose the preceding χ\chiχ nonnegative with support in (−1/2,1/2)(-1/2,1/2)(−1/2,1/2). The test (1+t0)χ(t0)ρ(t′)θ+(1+t_0)\chi(t_0)\rho(t')\theta_+(1+t0​)χ(t0​)ρ(t′)θ+​ is middle positive, hence weakly positive, whereas its pairing with TTT is −∫ρ<0-\int\rho<0−∫ρ<0. In particular one must not silently identify the two printed hypotheses.

For the standard real test space, nonnegativity on the middle positive cone is already a sufficient replacement for the order-zero conclusion. Indeed βp\beta^pβp lies in the full interior of that cone. On a fixed compact support, finite-dimensional cone domination bounds a symmetric test above and below by C∥η∥C0ζβpC\|\eta\|_{C^0}\zeta\beta^pC∥η∥C0​ζβp, with a fixed nonnegative smooth compact cutoff ζ\zetaζ equal to one on the support. Positivity then gives a coefficient C0C^0C0 bound; symmetry annihilates the antisymmetric part. This is precisely the distinction relevant to R, Convention 2.2, which chooses the middle cone of [CLD12, Definition 5.1.1(c)]. Neither this example nor its proof changes that internal input.

Scope of the obstruction.

The derivative distribution above is defined on an ordinary real tropical space. It has not been transported to a Berkovich skeleton. Such a transport would require control of all original refined tests, whose skeletal restrictions need not be smooth in these fixed coordinates. The original analytic counterexample in Example “A nonzero smooth closed current in the weak lineality space” remains a smooth, order-zero closed current. The present stronger non-Radon statement is confined to the real tropical setting, and neither example asserts that the quotient theorem is false for every possible weak-positive background class.

The excluded estimate.

The example rules out any general estimate whose hypotheses are only one uniform bound on the two classical decompositions, weak vanishing of their ambient curvature difference, and strong convergence in all fixed relative energy spaces, and whose conclusion is vanishing of the relative curvature differences. It also rules out obtaining the desired quotient by simply replacing actual classical differences with the full linear local energy domains. The function 1Yq\mathbf1_Yq1Y​q is an energy vector for every such background and annihilates all ambient smooth current tests, but it does not annihilate D(ϕ[Y])D(\phi[Y])D(ϕ[Y]). Therefore an approximation of those latter functionals in the dual of the unrestricted linear energy space cannot hold in general. Any successful energy argument must preserve an additional property of the actual classical differences; normal trace or a genuine regularity conclusion cannot be discarded in completion.

A necessary distinction.

Being carried by a complete pole set does not by itself imply membership in the universal kernel. With the notation of Example “Uniform bounded psh decompositions and universal strong energy do not suffice”, f=1Yqf=\mathbf1_Yqf=1Y​q still satisfies [f]=0[f]=0[f]=0, but D(f[Y])=D(q[Y])=ℓ−1δ(0,ζ0,1)≠0.D(f[Y])=D(q[Y]) =\ell^{-1}\delta_{(0,\zeta_{0,1})}\ne0.D(f[Y])=D(q[Y])=ℓ−1δ(0,ζ0,1​)​=0. The finite selector proposition requires the displayed ambient pluriharmonic weights; it does not replace them by arbitrary bounded Borel or classical psh weights. Nor does it assert a classification of the whole Borel kernel, countable selector closure, or invariance under arbitrary changes on ambient null sets. In particular the discontinuous selector does not contradict existence of a continuous representative of the zero distribution: its ambient current already has the representative zero. It shows that universal relative curvature does not recover that continuous representative from arbitrary assigned actual Borel values.

The descended operation is not weakly continuous

Potential independence is a statement about exact equality of curvature currents. It gives no continuity assertion for the operation when those currents vary weakly. The following example keeps the background fixed and makes both the approximating curvatures and their common ambient limit original smooth.

The convergence in (eq:r5-two-intersection-exact-measure) concerns the relative measures D(ajS)D(a_jS)D(aj​S), not the ambient curvatures D[aj]D[a_j]D[aj​]. It makes no assertion that general C1 fails for this background or for arbitrary backgrounds. The arbitrary-background quotient remains valid; its hypothesis concerns two actual classical potentials, and the completed aaa here cannot be replaced by any such potential with the same relative curvature. Finite pluriharmonic adjustments cannot remove the two incompatible actual intersection values.

The finite-wall pairing theorem permits compatible piecewise smooth tests to be evaluated against closed positive currents. A failed Gauss-perturbation shortcut

One possible route to scalar kernel functoriality was to perturb a finite parameter tuple by arbitrarily small independent Gauss variables, hoping that the resulting parameter point would always be Abhyankar. Exact norm-profile stability would then avoid any limit with moving coefficient measures. The premise is false, even for one parameter over the original finite field KKK.

This is a failure of the proposed perturbation mechanism, not of scalar kernel functoriality. In the one-variable proof, the positive limiting radius supplies a different tool: the continuous potential obtained from the uniformly Cauchy truncated logarithms of the nested discs. Its full-fiber curvature is treated in Proposition “A continuous full-fiber potential at every nonrigid point”.

Status change from R4 and remaining proof boundaries

The general question (Q) in the last subsection of R4 was exactly D[u]=D[v]⇒D((u−v)S)=0D[u]=D[v]\Rightarrow D((u-v)S)=0D[u]=D[v]⇒D((u−v)S)=0 for every allowed fixed SSS. Its two stated unresolved gates were all-complete-extension curve testing and continuity of the actual bounded classical difference. Sections “Complete scalar extensions through one-variable fiber potentials”– “Algebraic neighborhoods for the continuity argument” prove those gates; Theorem “Potential independence for every fixed positive closed background” therefore changes that precise question from OPEN to PROVED, relative to the declared inputs.
